subject: Staged release: request for customer allowlist + automated rollback authority
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, ops@heliumhealth.com
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: staged-release failover allowlist + rollback authority

Hi Laura / Aditya —

Quick ask: Helium Health (external) is ready to move from private beta to a constrained production launch next week. Their contract includes a 99.95% uptime SLO and low-latency commitments for checkout flows. Given the risk profile and their reliance on our inference routes, Id like to request an operational exception that: 

- Allows Helium Health to be on an explicit staged-release allowlist (A/B group with auto-routing) for the initial launch window.
- Grants the on-call release owner (me) and a director (Laura) authority to trigger an automatic rollback/pin to the last-known-good model variant for this customer when telemetry thresholds are hit, without standard multi-team signoff.

Concretely, the proposed safe-guards in the attached playbook (staged-release-failover-playbook.pdf):
- Canary size: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes initial observation
- Failure condition: three 1-minute windows where p50 latency > 900ms OR error rate > 0.75%
- Action: automatic fallback to pinned variant + persistent pin for 24 hours; auto-unpin back to progressive rollout if no regressions after 24h
- Telemetry: token-level tracing + rollback audit log to be shared with customer and Legal upon request

Rishi, can you confirm these telemetry windows are observable from our console and whether automatic rollback will preserve in-flight requests or cause session resets?

Sylvia / Helium Ops, looping you in so youre aware of the proposed control plane behavior. We can tailor the allowlist to match your maintenance window if needed.

Asks: Laura — approval to proceed with this exception (I will operate the rollback/pin authority), Aditya/Rishi — confirm telemetry + safe thresholds. Ive attached the playbook and a snapshot of the expected telemetry dashboard.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: staged-release-failover-playbook.pdf (policy + steps), telemetry-dashboard-snapshot.png
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: staged-release failover allowlist + rollback authority

Marissa —

I support granting a temporary operational carve-out for Helium Health with the following guarded approvals and conditions:

1) Canary and observation
   - Approve 5% canary for 30 minutes. After that, if no regression we move to 25% for 2 hours before broader rollout.

2) Automated rollback triggers (must be deterministic)
   - Trigger on: three 1-minute buckets where p50 latency exceeds 900ms OR error rate > 0.75%.
   - On trigger: immediate routing switch to the last stable variant with a documented audit log entry.

3) Pinning and recovery
   - Pin the previous variant for 24 hours post-fallback. Any unpin requires sign-off from either myself or the SRE lead (Rishi).

4) Audit and sign-off
   - Legal wants a DocuSign acknowledgement for the exception; please route the exception form through the legal doc link before the start.

5) Communication
   - Marissa, you have authority to initiate the auto-fallback when criteria are met. But please inform Sales leadership and the SRE pager within 5 minutes of action.

Rishi: confirm telemetry retention and whether the rollback path will drain gracefully (i.e., preserve in-flight responses or at least retry semantics). If we see a stateful session issue, we need a fallback plan to maintain SLA for Helium while we roll forward.

Approve pending Rishi and Aditya confirmation. Keep the playbook attached and add an "exceptions" cover sheet for Legal.

— Laura Bennett
Director, Product Operations, Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com
From: Sylvia Eng <sylvia.eng@heliumhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: staged-release failover allowlist + rollback authority

Thanks for the heads up, Marissa. A couple clarifying items from Helium Ops: 

- In-flight requests: if you automatically route customers away mid-request, will the client retry or will users see a hard error? We need to avoid any degraded UX.
- Session tokens: will pinning to the old variant change the expected response schema or session tokens such that our frontend needs a refresh?
- Region routing: our traffic is mostly US-east; can you ensure the allowlist preserves region affinity?
- Audit logs: procurement will request a retention sample for at least 90 days. Can you confirm well provide the rollback events and telemetry snapshots?

Maintenance window: were open to the staged rollout during our maintenance window on Mon 2 Nov 02:00-04:00 UTC if that helps.

Ive attached a quick screenshot of the customer-side error patterns we saw in beta (telemetry-dashboard-snapshot.png).

Sylvia Eng
Engineering Manager, Helium Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sylvia Eng <sylvia.eng@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: staged-release failover allowlist + rollback authority

Sylvia — thanks for the questions. Short answers and the final plan below.

- In-flight requests: our runtime will attempt a graceful drain. For stateless text-generation calls we will finish the current token stream on the old variant when possible; if a hard route swap is required we return a 202 + retry hint. We will not intentionally cut an in-flight response mid-token.
- Session tokens/schema: there should be no schema changes between variants for this rollout. If we detect shape changes in the first canary bucket we will auto-fallback immediately and include a compatibility report in the audit.
- Region affinity: we will honor US-east affinity; allowlist rules will be region-aware.
- Audit logs: confirmed — we will persist rollback events and a telemetry snapshot for 90 days and share a forensic export to procurement on request.

Finalized controls (agreed):
- 5% canary for 30 minutes, then 25% for 2 hours if stable.
- Automatic fallback on three 1-minute windows where p50 > 900ms OR errors > 0.75%.
- Pin to previous variant for 24 hours; unpin only after sign-off from Laura or Rishi.
- Marissa authorized to initiate fallback/pin; will notify SRE and Sales leadership within 5 minutes.
- Legal: I will route the exception acknowledgement via DocuSign (link: https://docusign.example.com/transactions/ABC-987654) before the launch window.

Planned launch window: we can align the beginning of the staged release to Heliums maintenance window on 2026-11-02 02:00 UTC. Please confirm final sign-off and Ill enqueue the playbook run and exception form.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
